title: Implement snapshot signing and orchestrated rollback queue
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds signed backup manifests and a serialized rollback queue to prevent concurrent restores; introduces preflight signature validation and installer CLI helpers. No user-facing API changes except new private-installer CLI commands.
description:
Motivation: During a recent restore drill we observed two separate restores targeting the same tenant that overlapped and left the cluster in an inconsistent state when downstream post-restore hooks raced. This PR implements two complementary protections: (1) cryptographically signed backup manifests so operators can verify integrity and provenance before restoring, and (2) an orchestrated rollback/restore queue that serializes restores per-tenant and exposes explicit lock/lease state for operator visibility. Both are designed for Private installer customers (VPC/on-prem) where operators manage backup artifacts in object storage and must be able to audit and safely recover state.

Summary of changes: Added an ed25519-based signature format for backup manifests and verification logic in the installer operator; added a new RestoreQueue controller that enqueues restore requests and processes them serially per-tenant with TTL-based leases; updated Helm charts and the installer CLI to produce and consume signed manifests; added a small Terraform module to maintain backup metadata and manifest storage ACLs; added preflight validations that compare manifest version stamps and schema compatibility before attempting a restore; added idempotent migration guard to the DB migration runner so an interrupted upgrade/rollback does not reapply incompatible steps. Also improved logging and tracing fields for auditability.

Commits (high level):
- feat(backup): introduce manifest signing utilities and key management helpers
- feat(operator): implement RestoreQueue controller with per-tenant leases
- feat(cli): add rw-private backup sign and rw-private restore enqueue commands
- chore(helm): helm templates for signed-backup-secret and restore-queue CRD
- feat(terraform): add backup-metadata module + s3 manifest ACL example
- fix(migrations): make schema migrations idempotent and add preflight dry-run
- test: add unit/integration tests for signature verification and queue behavior

Files changed (high level):
- operator/controllers/restore_queue_controller.go (new)
- pkg/backup/signature.go (new)
- cmd/rw-private/backup_sign.go (new), cmd/rw-private/restore_enqueue.go (new)
- charts/private/templates/signed-backup-secret.yaml (new)
- charts/private/templates/restore-queue-crd.yaml (new)
- terraform/modules/backup-metadata/main.tf (new)
- installer/preflight/validate_manifest.go (modified)
- migrations/db/migrate.go (modified)
- tests/integration/restore_queue_test.go (new)
- docs/private/operator-restore.md (new)

Design notes and constraints: Signatures use ed25519 with a simple manifest JSON that includes backup_version, object_url, created_at, model_version and a manifest_version stamp. The operator accepts a configured public key or a KMS-sourced key; when no key is configured the system falls back to a permissive mode but logs a warning (operators are encouraged to enable strict mode via Helm values). The RestoreQueue persists state to the cluster (CRs) and uses an optimistic lease pattern: when a restore job is dequeued we create a RestoreLease CR with owner reference and a TTL; if a job fails the lease is released and the job can be retried. The queue serializes per-tenant only; different tenants can run restores concurrently. This keeps the blast radius constrained while removing human coordination from restores.

Preflight & safety: The preflight step validates the manifest signature, checks manifest_version compatibility against the running installer version, runs a dry-run of DB migrations in a sandbox namespace, and verifies object storage ACLs via the new Terraform module outputs. If any check fails the restore is rejected and the operator emits a human-readable remediation hint in the events and logs.

Testing & CI: Added unit tests for signature.MaxExpectedAge enforcement, integration tests that exercise the queue in a kind cluster (mocked S3), and an E2E that signs a manifest with a test key then attempts an invalid restore to confirm preflight blocks it. CI initially showed a flaky integration test on the lease TTL; I increased the test timeout and added retries. The final run passed all checks (build, lint, unit, integration, e2e).

Review thread summary: Carlos requested stricter default Helm values (changed default strictSignature: true) and an option to fallback to KMS-only mode; Maya asked for clearer error messages when signatures are missing and suggested adding an operator metric for queued_length (added exporter metric restore_queue_length). Evan asked for more comments around the idempotency guarantees in DB migrations and requested an additional unit test for the migration dry-run path (added). I addressed all review comments and pushed a final changelist that removed a noisy debug log in signature verification.

Operational notes for customers: The new Helm chart exposes values.private.installer.signature.strict (default true), values.private.installer.signature.publicKey (string or KMS reference), and values.private.installer.restoreQueue.enabled (default true). Upgrading clusters: operators should run the included preflight job (rw-private preflight verify-manifests) against a snapshot store to surface potential incompatibilities before enabling auto-restore. If strict signature mode is enabled, restores without valid signatures will be rejected — tenants must sign manifests using the rw-private CLI or an approved orchestration flow.

Security considerations: Private key material is never stored by the operator; only public keys or KMS references are allowed in Helm. The Terraform module includes optional bucket policies to enforce server-side encryption and object locking where available. We documented destructive recovery flows in docs/private/operator-restore.md; operators should rotate keys via documented rotation steps to avoid lockouts.

Migration path and rollback: This change is backwards-compatible for clusters that do not enable strict signature mode. For clusters enabling strict mode, operators must sign existing manifests or toggle strictSignature off temporarily while they sign artifacts. The RestoreQueue controller supports a controller-runtime annotation to force-evict a lease for emergency interventions.

Merge: After approvals from reviewers and a green CI run, this PR was merged to main via squash merge. Changelog and docs were included in the merge commit.
notes: Operator docs added and CLI helpers included; recommended staging rollout before enabling strict signature mode in production.
